key_points: Two police officers and five others died in a crash in Middlesbrough.
A fundraising page for the families of the deceased officers reached £500,000.
Twelve people have been arrested for offenses ranging from firearm possession to organized crime activities.
Four of the five deceased occupants in the Volkswagen Passat had previous criminal convictions.
Downing Street called on TikTok and other platforms to remove wrong-way driving videos after footage emerged of one of the teenagers who died.

title: Anger hits peak as Snowdon hikers refuse to queue
author: Cameron Henderson
content:
![Crowds of people queue to reach the summit of Snowdon](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000499425376_17875856570490_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bqeo_i_u9APj8RuoebjoAHtyX5rhseiWKOo9p9OQ-ymek.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Crowds of people queue to reach the summit of Snowdon](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000499425376_17875856570490_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bqeo_i_u9APj8RuoebjoAHtyX5rhseiWKOo9p9OQ-ymek.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Few British traditions are more sacred than the unspoken rule of forming an orderly queue.
But this age-old etiquette has been tested to breaking point in Snowdonia, where hikers have been warned not to skip the queue at the top of Wales’s highest mountain after a series of rows.
This summer has seen large crowds flock to climb Snowdon, also known as Yr Wyddfa, where people have reportedly been forced to wait more than an hour to reach the 3,560ft summit.
Responding to reports of disorderly behaviour, the Snowdonia authorities have urged those wanting to reach the metal plate, called a trig point, to wait their turn.
Alun H Jones, an area warden for the park, told the BBC that hikers should be “considerate and don’t skip the queue”.
Footage on social media has shown arguments breaking out between queue-jumpers and those patiently waiting for their chance to reach the metal plate that marks the mountain’s highest point.
A recent video posted by Marc Screeton, from Manchester, showed him being heckled as he ascended the summit by other hikers who shouted: “There’s a queue you know.”
He responded: “Imagine queuing on a mountain. No chance.”
Another video posted by Jay Rouse was captioned: “Won’t catch me hiking for two hours to spend 30 minutes queuing at the top.”
Pleasant climbing conditions have boosted tourist numbers to the national park, leading to bottlenecks at the foot of the stone steps that lead to the metal plate, where hikers pose for photos and videos.
The mountain is widely considered the busiest in Europe, drawing m 600,000 people to its peak every year. The website Snowdon Info warns that congestion is normally at its worst around the middle of the day during July and August, as well as on weekends and bank holidays.
The park authority is expected to review concerns about over-tourism at a meeting after the October half-term.
Rows over queue-jumping have split opinion among walkers, with some calling for the queue to be respected and others arguing that such restrictions should not apply to the great outdoors.
‘It’s not Alton Towers’
Tina Millard from West Bromwich said: “I don’t think that you should have to queue.
“It’s a mountain, you should just be able to go up and that’s it.
“We’re not at Alton Towers for a ride. It’s a mountain, it’s for everyone,” she added.
Carl Lynch from Dunstable, Bedfordshire, said: “It should be: ‘go up there, two minutes and then move on for everyone else’. Simple as that.”
In May, two hikers raising money for charity were loudly booed after skipping queues to reach the summit.
Jamie Richardson, 32, and Richard Thiedeman, 34, from Lincolnshire, climbed Snowdon as part of the Three Peaks challenge to support their friend who has motor neurone disease.
![People shouted 'there's a queue you know' as the charity hikers reached the summit](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000499431305_17875857056051_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bqcjp2jEhFvsPQ_1cOyNpafFEsDn7Cfh7vPSa20qiClTg.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
“I was getting booed and then there was a gentleman who was at the top, who had just had his photo taken and he physically tried to stop me,” Mr Richardson said.
He said he had just touched the summit point and heard someone say “you should be ashamed of yourself”.
Mr Richardson added: “There’s no policing of it at all, it is purely free will, if you want to queue you can.
“The queuing, that is just purely down to British culture traditions.”
A spokesman for the national park confirmed it was “a self-policing queue”.
A spokesman for North Wales Police said: “We are not aware of any reports to police of physical confrontations but will always investigate should any alleged offences be disclosed.
“As in any public place, we would urge all hikers to be respectful to one another.”
summary: Tensions have risen on the summit of Snowdon in Wales as large crowds and long wait times have led to disputes between hikers waiting in line and those refusing to queue. Snowdonia authorities and wardens have urged visitors to be considerate and wait their turn for the metal plate marking the peak, while opinions among walkers remain sharply divided over whether queuing etiquette belongs on a mountain. The self-policing queue has seen social media footage of arguments and heckling, prompting the park authority to plan a review of over-tourism concerns after the October half-term.
key_points: Large summer crowds have caused hikers to wait over an hour to reach the summit metal plate of Snowdon, Wales's highest mountain.
Snowdonia authorities and park wardens have urged visitors to respect the self-policing queue and avoid queue-jumping.
Social media footage has captured arguments, heckling, and boos directed at hikers who bypassed the lines.
Walkers are divided, with some arguing that queuing on a mountain is unnecessary while others insist on maintaining the tradition of waiting one's turn.
The national park authority is expected to review over-tourism concerns following a meeting after the October half-term.

title: Man arrested for arson after huge blaze rips through Gatwick car park
author: Niva Yadav
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/s3fs-public/thumbnails/image/2017/07/21/16/gatwick-airport-car-park.jpg?crop=8:5,smart&quality=75&auto=webp&width=1000)
![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png)
West Sussex Fire and Rescue were called to the scene at Caldyne Business Park in Rowfant just after 9pm on Saturday (August 22).
UK Power Network was forced to shut off power to more than 2,000 homes while eight fire engines tackled the blaze through the night.
A man has since been arrested on suspicion of arson and taken into custody.
The site is primarily used for people parking their cars on their way to Gatwick Airport. Several cars and high voltage equipment are believed to have been damaged in the fire.
Read More
However, no casualties have been reported.
One social media user said the “devastating fire” destroyed the livelihoods of many, including a car breakdown and recovery business based at the site.
At the time of the blaze, West Sussex Police said in a statement: “Power has been shut off to the immediate area, affecting a number of businesses and homes, and nearby roads remain closed as a precaution.
“A number of cars have also been damaged at a site used for holiday parking.
“Any affected consumers are advised to contact their operator directly.
“A man has been arrested on suspicion of arson and transported to custody.
“Anyone with any information about the incident is asked to report it online or call 101, quoting serial 1504 of 22/08.”
West Sussex Police have been approached for comment.
summary: A large fire ripped through a Gatwick Airport holiday parking site at Caldyne Business Park in Rowfant late Saturday night. West Sussex Fire and Rescue deployed eight fire engines to tackle the blaze, which caused power outages for over 2,000 homes and damaged several vehicles and high-voltage equipment. A man has been arrested on suspicion of arson in connection with the incident, and no casualties have been reported.
key_points: A massive fire broke out at Caldyne Business Park, a site primarily used for Gatwick Airport holiday parking.
Eight fire engines fought the blaze through the night, while UK Power Network shut off power to over 2,000 homes.
A man was arrested on suspicion of arson and taken into custody.
Several cars and high voltage equipment were damaged, but no casualties were reported.

title: Twelve people arrested after A66 crash that killed seven including two police officers
author: Raphael Boyd
content:
Twelve people have been arrested on suspicion of offences including being involved with organised crime as part of the investigation into events leading to a crash on the A66 that killed two police officers and five others.
Cleveland police confirmed that nine men and three women were detained by officers investigating the events that led up to PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough dying when a Volkswagen Passat travelling the wrong way on the A66 near Middlesbrough collided with their marked armed response vehicle. All five men who were in the second car, aged between 17 and 23, were pronounced dead at the scene.
Police said some of those arrested as part of the A66 investigation, whose ages range from 19 to 61, were suspected of various offences “ranging from possession of a firearm to participating in the activities of an organised crime group”, while adding that four of those killed in the car that hit the police vehicle had previous police convictions.
The arrests have come as part of a “wide-scale investigation into the criminality which took place” in the hours leading up to the crash, which has involved the help of officers and staff from Durham, Northumbria and North Yorkshire police forces.
As part of the investigation a Volvo XC60, believed to be associated with the activities of the passengers of the Volkswagen Passat, had been identified and recovered, police said.
Assistant Chief Constable Wayne Fox said his force had engaged in “a fast-moving and complex investigation, with significant links to serious and organised criminal activity” and claimed the “events of that tragic night will have a lasting and profound impact on the Cleveland area and the communities we seek to protect”.
He said: “We have a duty to respond to, and thoroughly investigate, the serious criminal activity that resulted in this fatal incident, and to bring all those responsible to justice. Our robust response will continue in the weeks and months to come, as we continue to tackle those that seek to cause harm to our communities and tackle serious and organised crime.
“Officers and staff across Cleveland have shown incredible resilience in continuing their work in the face of tragedy. Two of their colleagues lost their lives while serving the people of Cleveland and, while the impact will be felt by our people for a long time to come, they have continued to act with the utmost professionalism.
“I am also extremely grateful for the support we have received, and continue to receive, from the public of Cleveland and our wider police family.”
Cleveland police played down links between the crash and a reported increase in videos depicting dangerous driving being posted online, stating there was “no evidence to indicate that filming of the activities that took place on Friday night and Saturday morning has taken place for the purposes of TikTok”.
summary: Twelve people have been arrested on suspicion of offences including organized crime and firearm possession following an A66 crash that killed seven people, including two police officers. The collision occurred when a Volkswagen Passat traveling the wrong way struck a marked police vehicle, resulting in the deaths of the two officers and all five men inside the Passat. Cleveland police are conducting a wide-scale investigation into the criminal activity leading up to the fatal incident, with assistance from neighboring police forces.
key_points: Twelve individuals aged 19 to 61 were detained on suspicion of offences including organized crime and possession of a firearm.
The crash killed seven people, including police officers PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough, and five men aged 17 to 23 in the second car.
Four of the men who died in the vehicle that hit the police car had previous police convictions.
A Volvo XC60 associated with the passengers of the Volkswagen Passat was identified and recovered during the investigation.
Police stated there is no evidence that the events leading to the crash were filmed for TikTok.

title: Ukraine’s allies convene in Kyiv as Zelenskyy seeks air defence boost
author: Al Jazeera Staff
content:
![Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham looks at Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky deliver a speech during a commemorative ceremony marking Ukraine's 35th Independence Day outside St. Sophia cathedral in Kyiv, Ukraine, August 24, 2026. HENRY NICHOLLS/Pool via REUTERS](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-24T104301Z_892133695_RC2Y4NASTE5M_RTRMADP_3_UKRAINE-CRISIS-COALITION-BURNHAM-1787569192.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
Ukraine will host a meeting with its key European allies to discuss air defence and press for greater pressure on Moscow as Russia continues to escalate missile attacks.
The “Coalition of the Willing” meeting in Kyiv will be jointly chaired by the leaders of France and Germany, who will join remotely, and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who arrived in the Ukrainian capital early on Monday.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Photos: Ukraine celebrates National Flag Day
- list 2 of 3Russia, Ukraine trade attacks as Putin warns of ‘far more destructive’ hits
- list 3 of 3Putin warns Ukraine has opened ‘Pandora’s box’, rejects peace proposals
European Council President Antonio Costa is also attending in person.
![UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham lays flowers at the tomb of the unknown Ukrainian soldier during a ceremony at Ukraine's national military memorial cemetery as the country marks the 35th anniversary of its independence, in Hatne southwest of Kyiv on August 24, 2026 \[Henry Nicholls/Pool via Reuters\]](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-24T085935Z_1192808379_RC2W4NAHH1BG_RTRMADP_3_UKRAINE-CRISIS-COALITION-BURNHAM-1787566404.jpg?w=770&resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
Kyiv is expected to seek additional interceptor missiles from allies after weeks of Russian missile and drone attacks that have driven record numbers of the capital city’s residents to metro stations and basements to seek shelter.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has made frequent public appeals for more air defence supplies from allies.
The meeting takes place on Ukraine’s Independence Day and comes a day after the country marked National Flag Day, when a group of leaders from Nordic and Baltic countries met Zelenskyy in Kyiv and pledged to boost their support for Ukraine.
Norway said it would provide another 85 billion kroner ($9.1bn) in 2027, matching the support it gave Ukraine this year.
Escalating air attacks
Russia and Ukraine have escalated air attacks with drones and missiles in recent weeks, striking targets far beyond the front line.
Ukraine has increasingly targeted Russian logistics sites, carrying out attacks on locations linked to e-commerce companies Wildberries and Ozon.
Ozon reported fires early on Monday at its warehouses in four cities including Krasnodar and Makhachkala, both in southern Russia, adding that sites in Adygeysk and Nevinnomyssk were evacuated due to threats of drone attack.
Russian authorities said two children were killed and nine other people were wounded, including seven minors, when drone debris hit a private childcare centre in Krasnodar on Monday. Debris also fell on apartment buildings and set warehouses alight in the city, Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said.
In the Stavropol region, which hosts many chemical production facilities, Governor Vladimir Vladimirov said a drone attack on an industrial area had been repelled early on Monday.
In Ukraine, at least two women were killed and five people injured when a Russian drone hit an electric train in the Kharkiv region on Sunday, regional officials said. An attack on the outskirts of Kharkiv city killed three people and injured eight.
Ukraine’s allies have pledged to boost Ukraine’s depleted air defences in the face of Russia’s growing missile attacks.
Before the meeting, Zelenskyy said deliveries of crucial Patriot interceptors had halved since 2023.
“Over the entire of 2023, Ukraine received 675 missiles, and over all of 2025 – 364, even though Russian missile strikes have increased,” he said.
“For 2026, as currently projected, it is 264,” he added, saying Ukraine was seeking a package of at least 300 for the upcoming winter.
summary: Ukraine is hosting key European allies in Kyiv for a "Coalition of the Willing" meeting to discuss air defence enhancements and increased pressure on Moscow amid escalating missile attacks. The meeting coincides with Ukraine's 35th Independence Day and follows recent pledges of financial and military support from Nordic, Baltic, and other European leaders. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is pressing allies for additional interceptor missiles as deliveries have steadily decreased since 2023.
key_points: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and European Council President Antonio Costa are attending the Kyiv meeting in person, while the leaders of France and Germany are joining remotely.
Ukraine is seeking a package of at least 300 Patriot interceptor missiles for the upcoming winter, noting that deliveries have dropped from 675 in 2023 to a projected 264 for 2026.
Norway recently pledged an additional 85 billion kroner ($9.1bn) in support for Ukraine in 2027.

Recent escalations in air attacks have resulted in casualties and infrastructure damage on both sides, including drone strikes on Russian warehouses and childcare facilities, and a Russian drone strike on a Ukrainian electric train.

title: Minister tells social media firms to remove posts that ‘celebrate’ dangerous driving after A66 crash
author: Raphael Boyd
content:
A minister has pressed social media companies to remove content from their platforms showcasing dangerous driving after a fatal collision that killed seven people in Middlesbrough.
The crash in the early hours of Saturday, in which PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough died, occurred when a Volkswagen Passat, containing five individuals aged between 23 and 17, crashed head-on with a marked armed response vehicle while driving the wrong way on the A66.
The five people in the Passat: Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Theo Rae, 17, Makai Saddington, 18, and Michael Robert Cahill, 23 and Jacob Matusiak, 23 were also pronounced dead at the scene.
The Passat was being pursued by police, who began following it after receiving intelligence of “multiple incidents” related to a vehicle matching its description. Police chased the car for seven minutes before it started to drive against the flow of traffic on the A66, at which point officers aborted the pursuit and remained on the correct side of the carriageway.
The car, which is believed to have had cloned plates, then collided with PC Blades and PC Clough’s vehicle about 10 seconds later.
Concerns have been raised about a link between the incident and videos that appear on social media platforms showing intentionally dangerous driving such as travelling the wrong way, filmed by the occupants of the cars and posted online.
Defence minister Luke Pollard has urged social media platforms to “step up” and remove posts that promote or encourage dangerous driving, which have become prevalent.
Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, Pollard said that his department had “communicated to those social media platforms that have been hosting content that celebrates this type of dangerous behaviour on our roads to take down that content.
“I think we all need to give the police time, but there’s also things we can be doing in the meantime to make sure that the internet is a safer place for everyone, that doesn’t celebrate and load views and therefore financial incentives on people to generate such awful content. I want to see social media companies step up.
“It’s one of the reasons they’ve argued against some of the regulations, saying they can police themselves. Well this is the perfect opportunity to demonstrate it. Remove the content that celebrates dangerous behaviour on our roads.”
Pollard added: “While that content is online, the government will be using the powers in the Online Safety Act to compel the platforms to take it down.
“But if the social media platforms were to regulate themselves and remove it in the first place, not allow their algorithm to share this type of content, because they know exactly what type of content that algorithm is designed to share, then I think we’d be in a better place.”
![Garda vehicles by two crumpled cars on a motorway.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/828db9bc76e63b5bf10417f9a8ff35fb5aaa2dfb/495_49_3385_2401/master/3385.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
An Ofcom spokesperson said social media platforms were required under the Online Safety Act to minimise children’s exposure to content that encourages dangerous stunts and challenges, with TikTok already under investigation by the regulatory body due to worries about the effectiveness of its age-checking software.
They said: “Under the Online Safety Act, platforms must minimise children’s exposure to violent material and content promoting dangerous challenges.
“In July, we launched an investigation into TikTok’s compliance with its child safety duties, and we’ve shown we’ll take action if evidence suggests companies are falling short.”
TikTok has denied that its content puts children at risk, claiming that it prohibits content that could cause significant physical harm, including dangerous driving, from being viewed, and that it removes any videos and accounts that break its rules.
The A66 crash came just under a week after five teenagers died in a crash involving a car driving in the wrong direction on a motorway in Ireland. A vehicle driving the wrong way of the M9 in County Kildare collided with a car containing four people, all of whom were hospitalised with serious injuries.
summary: Following a fatal head-on collision on the A66 that killed seven people, including two police officers, a government minister has urged social media companies to remove online content that celebrates dangerous driving. The crash occurred when a Volkswagen Passat traveling the wrong way collided with a police vehicle during a police pursuit. Defence minister Luke Pollard stated that the government will use the Online Safety Act to compel platforms to take down such material if they fail to remove it voluntarily.
key_points: A fatal head-on crash on the A66 in Middlesbrough resulted in the deaths of seven individuals, including two police officers and five occupants of a Volkswagen Passat.
The Passat had been traveling the wrong way against traffic during a police pursuit.
Defence minister Luke Pollard called on social media platforms to remove videos celebrating dangerous driving.
The government warned it will use powers under the Online Safety Act to force platforms to take down dangerous driving content if they do not self-regulate.

title: Police investigate rape of girl,14, in trees off Swaythling roundabout
author: Indy Almroth-Wright
content:
![Police car and tape across a wooded area off a roundabout with a sign to Swaythling.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/af7e/live/ec33e870-9f9e-11f1-a83c-33ebef033ca4.jpg)
The teenage girl reported being attacked on Sunday afternoon near the Wide Lane roundabout
- Published
Police have set up a cordon in a wooded area after a 14-year-old girl reported being raped by a man she did not know.
The girl reported the attack happened in an area of trees off the Wide Lane roundabout, near Mansbridge Road in Southampton, shortly before 15:10 BST on Sunday. She is being supported by specialist officers.
Hampshire police said the man, aged in his 30s or 40s was reported to be tall, skinny, with slicked back blonde, greasy "curtain-style" hair with inch-long beard hair, pale/sandy skin and an arm tattoo that looks like writing.
The force is urging anyone who recognises the description or has CCTV, doorbell or dashcam footage from the area at the time to come forward.
Det Supt Ross Toms said the "very detailed description of the man" described his clothes as blue skinny jeans, a dark short-sleeved top that was short at the back and beige or white plimsoll-style shoes.
Toms said: "This incident was understandably very distressing for the girl involved. Our specialist officers are supporting her while we have significant resources in the area thoroughly investigating this incident as a priority.
"If you saw or heard anything in this area between the times stated, no matter how small your information could be crucial so please contact police."
The force said said officers would be in Swaythling speaking to residents and checking CCTV footage.
summary: Hampshire police are investigating the reported rape of a 14-year-old girl by an unknown man in a wooded area off the Wide Lane roundabout in Southampton. The attack occurred shortly before 15:10 BST on Sunday, and the victim is currently receiving support from specialist officers. Authorities have cordoned off the area and are urging anyone with information, CCTV, or dashcam footage to come forward.
key_points: A 14-year-old girl reported being raped in a wooded area off the Wide Lane roundabout in Southampton on Sunday afternoon.
The suspect is described as a tall, skinny man in his 30s or 40s with blonde 'curtain-style' hair, an inch-long beard, pale skin, and an arm tattoo resembling writing.
The suspect was reportedly wearing blue skinny jeans, a dark short-sleeved top, and beige or white plimsoll-style shoes.
Police have deployed significant resources to the area, are checking CCTV, and are asking residents for any relevant footage or information.

title: Five children rescued at Shoebury beach amid rising tide
author: Rachael McMenemy
content:
![An orange hovercraft glides across wet sand with some areas completely covered in water amid a rising tide. There are two people on the hovercraft.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1800/cpsprodpb/435b/live/2d8b3a20-9f82-11f1-82a0-8dbe1008b861.jpg)
Southend-on-Sea RNLI launched their hovercraft to bring the children back to shore
- Published
Five children were rescued half a mile (0.8km) offshore as the tide rose around them.
They were reported at Shoebury Boom on Shoebury East Beach in Essex at 16:45 BST on Sunday.
Southend-on-Sea RNLI launched its hovercraft and brought the cold but uninjured children back to shore and their waiting parents.
"They could have come into real danger quickly. With no way of calling for help, improper footwear and an unfamiliarity with the area, today's call could have had a very different outcome," warned RNLI volunteer Commander Jonathan Charnock.
"Southend has a vast tidal flat area, at low tide the water can be over one mile from the shore. East Beach has the added danger of the Ministry of Defence (MoD) firing range to the east of the Boom," Charnock added.
He urged people to check the local area and ensure they always have a way to call for help when visiting beaches.
Do you have a story suggestion for Essex? Contact us below.
summary: Five children were rescued by the Southend-on-Sea RNLI hovercraft after becoming stranded half a mile offshore by a rising tide at Shoebury East Beach in Essex. The children were cold but uninjured when brought back to shore to their parents. RNLI officials warned that the situation could have ended differently due to the lack of communication devices, improper footwear, and unfamiliarity with the area's vast tidal flats.
key_points: Five children were rescued half a mile offshore at Shoebury East Beach.
Southend-on-Sea RNLI used a hovercraft to bring the children back to shore.
The children were cold and uninjured, and were reunited with their parents.
RNLI volunteers highlighted dangers including vast tidal flats, an MoD firing range, and the children having no way to call for help.

title: Burnham in Ukraine with plans to hand over UK blueprints for long-range missiles - follow live
author: Live Reporting Edited by Angus Thompson
content:
![](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/128/cpsprodpb//vivo/live/images/2026/8/24/a7fda7a1-47a1-4e54-b0f7-3cb508bb1768.jpg.webp) Vitaly Shevchenko
Chief analyst, BBC Monitoring
Russia's commissioner for children's rights, Maria Lvova-Belova, says three teenagers (aged 13, 15 and 16) have been killed in a Ukrainian attack on southern Krasnodar territory.
In a statement on social media, she says six other children were taken to hospital with shrapnel wounds, burns and concussions.
According to the local governor, Veniamin Kondratyev, a centre for children in Krasnodar was hit by "drone debris".
Lvova-Belova and Vladimir Putin are wanted by the International Criminal Court at the Hague for allegedly committing the war crime of unlawful deportation of children from occupied parts of Ukraine.
Separately, Ukrainian drones attacked three warehouses belonging to Ozon, a Russian online retail platform - in Adygeya, Makhachkala and Krasnodar. Russian state news agency TASS says several people were injured in the attack on the Ozon warehouse in Makhachkala, but their lives are not believed to be in danger.
The strikes on Ozon follow repeated Ukrainian drone attacks against warehouses belonging to Wildberries, another major Russian online retail platform.
Robert Brovdi, the commander of the Ukrainian drone forces, also says they hit a Russian MiG-29 fighter jet in Rostov region.
According to the Russian defence ministry, a total of 351 Ukrainian drones were intercepted overnight.
summary: Three teenagers were killed and six other children were injured in a Ukrainian attack involving drone debris hitting a children's center in Russia's Krasnodar territory, according to Russian officials. Additionally, Ukrainian drones targeted three warehouses belonging to the Russian online retail platform Ozon, resulting in injuries in Makhachkala. Ukrainian forces also reportedly struck a Russian MiG-29 fighter jet in the Rostov region.
key_points: Three teenagers aged 13, 15, and 16 were killed in Krasnodar territory.
Six other children were hospitalized with shrapnel wounds, burns, and concussions.
Ukrainian drones attacked three warehouses belonging to Russian retailer Ozon.
A Russian MiG-29 fighter jet was reportedly hit in the Rostov region.
The Russian defence ministry stated that 351 Ukrainian drones were intercepted overnight.

title: Minister tells social media firms to take down dangerous driving content in wake of fatal A66 crash in Middlesborough – UK politics live
author: Yohannes Lowe; Vivian Ho
content:
A police cordon at the scene of a fatal crash involving a police car and a Volkswagen Passat on the A66 in South Bank, near Middlesbrough on Saturday. Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA
A police cordon at the scene of a fatal crash involving a police car and a Volkswagen Passat on the A66 in South Bank, near Middlesbrough on Saturday. Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA
Social media firms told to take down dangerous driving content in wake of fatal A66 crash
Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of UK politics. The government has told social media companies to take down content showing people driving the wrong way down roads following a fatal crash over the weekend.
Two police officers were among seven people killed when a car travelling the wrong way down a dual carriageway crashed into a force vehicle on the A66 near Middlesbrough.
There have been reports that at least one of the young men who died in the collision early on Saturday had been involved in filming dangerous driving in TikTok videos.
Asked about these reports this morning, the defence minister, Luke Pollard, said social media platforms must remove content glorifying dangerous driving or else the government will use powers under the Online Safety Act to compel them to take the videos down. Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live this morning, Pollard said:
We’ve communicated to those social media platforms that have been hosting content that celebrates this type of dangerous behaviour on our roads to take down that content.
I think we all need to give the police time, but there’s also things we can be doing in the meantime to make sure that the internet is a safer place for everyone, that doesn’t celebrate and load views and therefore financial incentives on people to generate such awful content. I want to see social media companies step up.
It’s one of the reasons they’ve argued against some of the regulations, saying they can police themselves. Well this is the perfect opportunity to demonstrate it. Remove the content that celebrates dangerous behaviour on our roads.
Five people were killed and four seriously injured after the collision on the M9 in County Kildare on 16 August 2026. Photograph: Niall Carson/PA
The issue of lax social media regulation of dangerous driving content came to prominence amid a public outcry in Ireland afterfive teenagers were killed in a head-on crash involving a car driving in the wrong direction on a motorway in County Kildare last weekend.
The Garda commissioner, Justin Kelly, described the head-on collision between the two cars as “horrific” and said “in some cases” vehicles were being driven on the wrong side of motorways for social media likes. TikTok declined an invitation to appear before an Irish parliamentary committee on media to discuss videos, citing the ongoing police investigation, according to Ireland’s national broadcaster, RTÉ,
The prime minister will use the trip to Kyiv to announce that the UK government will allow the European defence company MBDA to declassify information about UK-made components of the Anglo-French Storm Shadow/Scalp missiles to help Ukraine build its own version.
While the announcement will probably take years to have an impact on the war, it is likely to escalate tensions with Moscow at an already fraught moment in UK-Russian relations.
Andy Burnham will announce in Kyiv that the UK will help France set up assembly lines in Ukraine for long-range missiles, which the French president, Emmanuel Macron, promised last month.
The British announcement is a small step in a much larger and longer-term project that could lead to Ukraine making its own long-range versions of the Storm Shadow cruise missile in several years’ time.
Andy Burnham and Volodymyr Zelensky talking at HM Naval Base Portsmouth last month. Burnham’s visit to Kyiv on Monday is his first as prime minister. Photograph: Jason Alden/EPA
But the move is likely to trigger further criticism from Moscow at a time when tensions between the UK and Russia are already high.
Last week, Russia accused the UK of deliberately escalating the conflict by allowing Ukraine to launch attacks with British-made drones, warning that the deeper Britain’s involvement, “the higher the price it will pay”.
This weekend it emerged that Russia had withdrawn its ambassador in London without naming a replacement, prompting speculation it was downgrading its diplomatic presence in the UK.
Burnham has insisted that Russian threats will not weaken British support for Ukraine, saying last week: “We are not fair-weather friends. We will be there in Ukraine’s hour of need, and that won’t change.” You can read more from my colleagues Kiran StaceyandDan Sabbagh here:
Andy Burnham arrives in Ukraine with promise of boost for Kyiv’s long-range missiles
Vivian Ho
The prime minister, Andy Burnham, arrived in the Ukrainian capital Kyiv on Monday alongside a number of European leaders to mark the country’s independence day.
Burnham was photographed at Kyiv railway station shaking hands with Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha, who said Burnham was to be joined by António Costa, president of the European Council; Luc Frieden, the prime minister of Luxembourg; Maia Sandu, the president of Moldova; and Alar Karis, the president of Estonia.
Ukraine’s foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, prepares to greet Andy Burnham upon his arrival by train in Kyiv on 24 August 2026. Photograph: Henry Nicholls/Reuters
“For Ukraine, independence is not an abstract idea. We defended it against all odds. In times like these, nations learn how important it is to have allies by your side,” Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said in a post on X announcing their arrival.
“And today, we know for sure who our true friends are.”
Burnham plans to announce during his visit that the UK government will allow the European defence company MBDA to declassify information about UK-made components of the Anglo-French Storm Shadow/Scalp long-range missiles to help Ukraine build its own version – a major boost to the country’s capacity in weapons development at a crucial time in the war. You can read the latest developments in our Europe live blog:
Cleveland police and crime commissioner Matt Storey was on BBC Radio 4’s Today programme this morning to take questions on the fatal A66 crash.
Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Theo Rae, 17, Makai Saddington, 18, and 23-year-olds Michael Robert Cahill and Jacob Matusiak died when their Volkswagen Passat, believed to be using cloned plates, collided with a marked armed response vehicle early on Saturday near Middlesbrough.
Pc Matthew Blades, 37, and Pc Tom Clough, 38, who had been driving in the correct direction, were killed in the collision. They have been hailed as heroes by their families.
PC Tom Clough (left) and PC Matthew Blades, who died when a car going in the wrong direction hit a police car on the A66 near Middlesbrough. Photograph: Cleveland Police/PA
It has been reported that Saddington was involved in filming dangerous driving in TikTok videos before the fatal crash took place – although this has not been confirmed by police. Storey acknowledged the reports about the TikTok videos, but urged people to avoid speculation. He said:
Without being able to say whether that was anything like involved in this case, it’s absolutely idiotic for anybody to be doing anything other than being completely 100% focused on the road when they’re behind the wheel of a vehicle.
And for somebody to be filming themselves or doing anything like that is absolutely ridiculous, and of course nobody should be doing that. And it is a worrying situation if that’s becoming more prevalent because it is incredibly dangerous.

Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live this morning, Pollard said:

I think we all need to give the police time, but there’s also things we can be doing in the meantime to make sure that the internet is a safer place for everyone, that doesn’t celebrate and load views and therefore financial incentives on people to generate such awful content. I want to see social media companies step up.

Five people were killed and four seriously injured after the collision on the M9 in County Kildare on 16 August 2026. Photograph: Niall Carson/PA
The issue of lax social media regulation of dangerous driving content came to prominence amid a public outcry in Ireland afterfive teenagers were killed in a head-on crash involving a car driving in the wrong direction on a motorway in County Kildare last weekend.
The Garda commissioner, Justin Kelly, described the head-on collision between the two cars as “horrific” and said “in some cases” vehicles were being driven on the wrong side of motorways for social media likes. TikTok declined an invitation to appear before an Irish parliamentary committee on media to discuss videos, citing the ongoing police investigation, according to Ireland’s national broadcaster, RTÉ,
summary: The UK government has warned social media companies to remove content glorifying dangerous driving, such as driving the wrong way down roads, following a fatal crash on the A66 near Middlesbrough. Seven people died in the collision, including two police officers and five occupants of a Volkswagen Passat, amid reports that at least one of the deceased individuals may have filmed dangerous driving for TikTok. Defence minister Luke Pollard stated that powers under the Online Safety Act will be used to compel platforms to remove the videos if they fail to comply.
key_points: Seven people, including two police officers and five individuals in a Volkswagen Passat, were killed in a head-on collision on the A66 near Middlesbrough.
Reports indicated that at least one of the young men who died may have been involved in filming dangerous driving videos for TikTok.
Defence minister Luke Pollard urged social media platforms to remove content celebrating dangerous driving or face government compulsion via the Online Safety Act.
The issue has drawn broader concern following a similar fatal crash in County Kildare, Ireland, where five teenagers died after a car was driven in the wrong direction for social media likes.

title: Burnham hands Storm Shadow blueprints to Ukraine
author: Joe Barnes
content:
![Prime Minister Andy Burnham speaks with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky during their visit to HM Naval Base in Portsmouth on July 27, 2026](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000496705723_17875156986650_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqDPfUJJJzp2bObtoYsJdDTv4Xpit_DMGvdp2n7FDd82k.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Prime Minister Andy Burnham speaks with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky during their visit to HM Naval Base in Portsmouth on July 27, 2026](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000496705723_17875156986650_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqDPfUJJJzp2bObtoYsJdDTv4Xpit_DMGvdp2n7FDd82k.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Andy Burnham will hand Ukraine secret blueprints for Storm Shadow missiles on his first visit to the country as Prime Minister.
He has agreed to release classified information on British components so that Kyiv can manufacture the long-range weapon for use in its war against Russia.
The latest show of support was announced on Monday, when Mr Burnham and other world leaders arrived in the Ukrainian capital to mark the 35th anniversary of its independence from the Soviet Union.
“On Ukraine’s 35th anniversary of independence, the Ukrainian people should be in no doubt – the UK is behind you today and for as long as it takes,” Mr Burnham said.
“I am proud of the contribution our country has made to Ukraine, and I want the Ukrainian people to hear it directly from me that our support will not waver. After all, Ukraine’s security is our security.
“The friendship between our two countries will long outlast Russia’s illegal war. In both the fight and in the rebuilding to come, we will stand with Ukraine and deliver opportunities for people across both our countries.
“Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve. We will not back down until there is a just and lasting peace.”
![Mr Burnham shakes hands with Andrii Sybiha, the Ukrainian foreign minister, after arriving in Kyiv](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000499399824_17875540442640_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqHglMIiZKcnuDpqDyxlvx604eMDo-eeUoD6nOhkL24pU.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Later in the day, the Prime Minister will meet Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukraine’s president, and chair a meeting of the “coalition of the willing”.
France agreed to hand over the blueprints for its Scalp-EG – the export name for Storm Shadow missiles – to Ukraine as part of a wider defence deal struck in July.
However, Ukraine’s ability to manufacture the missile domestically hinged on a British decision to allow the European missile maker MBDA to release sensitive information on UK-made components.
![Mr Burnham met Luc Frieden, the prime minister of Luxembourg, while travelling to Kyiv](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000499399803_17875540440313_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqgsaO8O78rhmZrDxTlQBjdLdu0TL-Cg_AMOUqySXmFgU.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
The British and French militaries gave the Ukrainians a limited number of Storm Shadow and Scalp-EG missiles, which have a range of around 150 miles and feature bunker-busting warheads.
The air-launched weapons have proven vital in Ukrainian strikes on heavily-fortified and hard to reach targets deep behind the frontlines, both on occupied territory and the Russian mainland.
Notably, Storm Shadows were used in separate strikes on Sevastopol, the Crimean port city, targeting the headquarters of Russia’s Black Sea Fleet and a submarine in September 2023.
They were first used on the Russian mainland a year later after Joe Biden, the former US president, lifted a Western veto on cross-border strikes using powerful missiles. The Trump administration reinstated the block, but lifted it again in October 2025.
The British-French missile relies on classified US targeting data to ensure it can hug terrain en route to the target.
It is not clear whether Washington would sign off and provide data for every strike Ukraine plans with domestically built Scalp-EG/Storm Shadow.
There is also no guarantee Ukraine would be able to begin manufacturing Scalp-EG/Storm Shadow immediately given the difficulties it will face setting up complex production lines
Mr Zelensky has been pushing for the production of Western weapons systems inside Ukraine to boost and accelerate deliveries to Kyiv’s armed forces.
The British and French decisions to trust Ukraine with sensitive blueprints could convince other Western allies to follow suit.
Donald Trump had promised Ukraine a licence to produce Patriot surface-to-air interceptor missiles, which it desperately needs to defend against incoming Russian ballistic missiles.
But the process has been delayed over fears the technology could fall into Russian hands, with the US president appearing to backtrack on the promise in July.
Mr Zelensky said on Saturday that Ukraine had requested 360 Patriot missiles from allies, but hoped to receive 300.
![A Patriot interceptor missile being fired](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499370581_17875168345600_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqdNLuJDSj-bduoIdVkVeVwZgojZYlP8f0i9h2tPqCNsM.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Russia has significantly stepped up its deadly long-range attacks on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities amid shortages of the US-made interceptors, which is the only reliable weapon for shooting down ballistic missiles.
The Ukrainian president said the supply of interceptors and a $27bn (£19.8bn) financial blackhole faced by his ministry of defence were the country’s two “major challenges”.
He added that he was working with France and Germany to release €30bn (£25.7bn) in funding from the European Union, which is being held up by demands for legislative reforms in Kyiv.
The British move to push through Ukrainian production of Scalp-EG is likely to trigger a further deterioration in diplomatic relations with Moscow.
On Sunday, the Kremlin revealed that it had withdrawn Andrei Kelin, its long-serving ambassador to London, after seven years in the UK.
Announcing the move, a spokesman for Russia’s foreign ministry accused Britain of opting for a “path of confrontation” and urged the Government to “reconsider its policies towards our country”.
![Russian Ambassador Andrei Kelin appearing on the BBC 1 current affairs programme, Sunday With Laura Kuenssberg on May 28, 2023](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000337459341_17875158797450_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqnZlAO2SbRIMsCE2ccfSvVJgojZYlP8f0i9h2tPqCNsM.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Last week, Moscow threatened undefined “consequences” when it emerged British-made drones had been used by Ukraine to strike targets on Russian soil.
Western intelligence sources have told The Telegraph that Russia has launched a fresh wave of attacks on European armaments factories under the guise of plausible deniability.
A spate of fires and explosions have been reported at plants in Estonia, Italy and Bulgaria, where drones and ammunition were being manufactured for Ukraine.
The Kremlin is recruiting local gang members to sabotage defence manufacturers to test Nato’s resolve.
The attacks appear carefully calculated to fall just short of triggering Article 5, Nato’s mutual defence clause, intelligence officials believe.
A Nato official told the Telegraph: “In recent years, Russia has accelerated its destabilisation campaigns against Allies through cyber attacks, assassination attempts and acts of sabotage.”
What has become known as the Kremlin’s “hybrid war”, different officials argue, is aimed at escalating tensions among Nato’s allies and deterring support for Ukraine.
The Nato official added: “Nato continues to boost its resilience and is applying and enhancing the tools at our disposal to counter hybrid actions. We continue to monitor malign activities conducted against Allies, including through proxies.
“At every stage, we will ensure that the Alliance is prepared to deter and defend against any threat and to keep our one billion citizens safe.”
summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced during a visit to Kyiv that the UK will share secret blueprints for the Storm Shadow missile with Ukraine. The decision allows Ukraine to domestically manufacture the long-range weapon, which relies on British components. The move coincides with Ukraine's 35th independence anniversary and follows a similar agreement by France regarding its Scalp-EG missiles.
key_points: Prime Minister Andy Burnham visited Kyiv to mark Ukraine's 35th independence anniversary and announced the transfer of Storm Shadow blueprints.
The agreement enables Ukraine to manufacture the long-range missiles domestically, contingent on sensitive information regarding UK-made components.
France previously agreed to hand over blueprints for its equivalent Scalp-EG missile as part of a defense deal.
The British move is expected to cause a further deterioration in diplomatic relations with Moscow, following Russia's withdrawal of its ambassador to London.

title: Moscow withdraws UK ambassador as tensions between Britain and Russia mount
author: Athena Stavrou
content:
Moscow has withdrawn its UK ambassador as relations between Britain and Russia continue to deteriorate amid Vladimir Putin’s war in Ukraine.
Andrey Kelin, who had been in the role for more than seven years, left his post on 21 July.
According to The Times, Russia is yet to submit another candidate to the Foreign Office and there is reportedly no indication of when a replacement may be appointed.
The Russian embassy in London denied Russia intends to downgrade diplomatic relations between Moscow and Britain, but said ties have “deteriorated to an unprecedentedly low level entirely on London's initiative”.
A spokesperson for the Russian embassy told The Times that the former ambassador had made “considerable efforts to preserve contacts and channels of communication” with the UK but accused the government of choosing a “path of confrontation” with Russia.
![It is unclear why Kelin left his post after a seven-year tenure](https://static.independent.co.uk/2022/11/03/19/b947008e230909ba4106b578d9e872daY29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNjY3NTg4MjMy-2.65503259.jpg)
“He left Britain in the hope that a more constructive and respectful dialogue could eventually be restored, should the UK reconsider its policies towards our country,” the spokesperson said.
“In the meantime, the embassy is headed by the chargé d’affaires.”
A Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office spokesperson said: “This is a matter for the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
“We have an ambassador and embassy in Moscow to engage and raise concerns with the Russian government.
“We continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine, which has the right to defend itself against Russia’s illegal and unprovoked invasion.”
Last week, Russia’s embassy in the UK said reports that Ukrainian forces had used unmanned aircraft manufactured by two UK companies “confirm that London is deliberately opting for an escalation of the Ukraine crisis”.
It accused Britain of “seeking to contain Russia and inflict maximum damage on it by proxy” and warned that the deeper its involvement becomes, “the higher the price it will pay”.
“London’s actions will inevitably carry consequences for which it will have to answer,” it said.
But prime minister Andy Burnham hit back, saying Britain would not be deterred by the threats.
Asked what his message to Putin was after Russia accused the UK of escalating the war, Mr Burnham said: “This is the UK doing what it has long said it would do, which is to support Ukraine 100 per cent against this illegal war led by Vladimir Putin.
“We are providing support so that Ukraine can defend itself, and that’s been the British position all the way through this conflict by previous prime ministers.
“It remains the case with me. We are not fair-weather friends. We will be there in Ukraine’s hour of need, and that won’t change.”
It is unclear why Mr Kelin left his post after his seven-year tenure. Last year, he denied Russian involvement in the 2018 Salisbury poisonings, claiming they were “staged” in a plot reminiscent of an Agatha Christie novel.
summary: Moscow has withdrawn Andrey Kelin, its ambassador to the UK, following years of deteriorating relations amid the war in Ukraine. Russia has not yet announced a replacement, leaving the embassy headed by a chargé d'affaires, though the embassy denied intentions to downgrade diplomatic ties. Meanwhile, tensions have been further inflamed by Russian accusations that Britain is escalating the conflict by supplying Ukraine, a claim rejected by British leadership.
key_points: Russian ambassador to the UK Andrey Kelin left his post on 21 July after more than seven years in the role.
Russia has not yet named a replacement candidate to the Foreign Office.
The Russian embassy blamed the UK for deteriorating relations, accusing London of choosing a path of confrontation.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated that Britain will remain committed to supporting Ukraine despite Russian threats and warnings.

title: Burnham to hand long-range missile blueprints as he visits Kyiv
author: Henry Moore
content:
![Andy Burnham and Volodymyr Zelensky walk next to each other at a naval base. Both men are dressed in black and have short, dark hair. Burnham is wearing glasses. Military personnel can be seen in the background.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/800/cpsprodpb/fb9a/live/545c7720-9ef8-11f1-aed4-af6fe65bfcd6.jpg)
Andy Burnham (left) and Volodymyr Zelensky during a recent visit to Portsmouth
- Published
Andy Burnham is marking his first foreign visit as prime minister with a trip to Kyiv - and will hand over blueprints so Ukraine can build its own long-range missiles.
The prime minister will chair his first meeting of the "coalition of the willing", set up by the UK and France under his predecessor, Sir Keir Starmer.
He is also set to accept an award on behalf of the British people recognising the UK's support for Ukraine and to take part in independence day events.
Crucially for the war effort, he will announce his government has agreed to allow defence company MBDA to declassify information on UK components for the long-range Scalp missile â the French equivalent of the UK's Storm Shadow.
Burnham will be reaffirming the UK's backing for Kyiv in the wake of escalating Russian strikes on Ukraine in recent weeks - including one on a shopping centre on Friday that killed at least 16 people.
Ahead of his visit on Monday, Burnham said: "On Ukraine's 35th anniversary of independence, the Ukrainian people should be in no doubt: the UK is behind you today and for as long as it takes.
"I am proud of the contribution our country has made to Ukraine and I want the Ukrainian people to hear it directly from me that our support will not waver. After all, Ukraine's security is our security."
He said the friendship Ukraine shared with the UK would "long outlast Russia's illegal war", adding: "Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve. We will not back down until there is a just and lasting peace."
It comes after Moscow warned of "consequences" over the use of British drones by Ukraine in its recent ramping up of strikes on Russian infrastructure.
Kyiv has stepped up long-range attacks on Moscow and other Russian regions, targeting oil refineries and warehouses of the country's largest online retailer, Wildberries.
Watch: Burnham pledges support in first meeting with Zelensky
The Russian embassy in the UK has accused Britain of "deliberately opting for an escalation of the Ukraine crisis", saying "the deeper its involvement in the conflict... the higher the price it will pay".
In response, Burnham said last week: "We are not fair-weather friends, we will be there in Ukraine's hour of need and that won't change."
Asked on Tuesday about the Russian threat, Burnham maintained the UK was "providing support so that Ukraine can defend itself and that's been the British position all the way through this conflict, by previous prime ministers - it remains the case with me".
The visit comes as Russia confirmed its ambassador to the UK, Andrei Kelin, had left his post in London in recent weeks.
The Kremlin is yet to put forward a replacement but Russia's embassy to the UK told the BBC it did not reflect an intention to downgrade diplomatic relations between the two nations.

During his visit, he will hand over blueprints allowing Ukraine to build its own long-range missiles and chair his first meeting of the "coalition of the willing." Burnham also plans to accept an award on behalf of the British people and participate in independence day events.

He will provide blueprints enabling Ukraine to build its own long-range missiles by declassifying information on UK components for the Scalp missile.
Burnham will chair his first meeting of the "coalition of the willing" and accept an award recognising UK support for Ukraine.

title: Light aircraft pilot seriously injured in crash
author: Samuel Montgomery
content:
![An aerial view of the airfield in Hampshire](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499379959_17875229935290_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq1ke4BK-zb_Zwill9XROpnLrNfJAuyPmNt1Dc1MaT2YU.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![An aerial view of the airfield in Hampshire](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499379959_17875229935290_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq1ke4BK-zb_Zwill9XROpnLrNfJAuyPmNt1Dc1MaT2YU.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
A pilot has been seriously injured after crashing his light aircraft at an airfield in Hampshire.
The 62-year-old man sustained “potentially life-threatening” injuries after the plane he was flying “overturned” at Popham Airfield on Sunday evening.
Emergency services managed to free the man from the wreckage and took him to Southampton Hospital by road ambulance.
A spokesman for Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said the man had sustained “serious and potentially life-threatening and life-changing injuries”.
The first 999 call was reportedly made at 5.43pm following reports of a microlight crashing with the pilot trapped inside.
The first ambulance crew is said to have arrived at the scene just 16 minutes later at 5.59pm.
An air ambulance, critical care doctors and firefighters were also deployed to the airfield.
The firefighters worked to release the man from the aircraft before handing him over to paramedics, who took him to Southampton Hospital at 7.02pm.
A spokesman for Hampshire Police said: “We were called at 5.45pm with reports of a collision at Popham Airfield involving a single light aircraft which had overturned.
“The pilot, a man aged in his 60s, has sustained serious and potentially life-threatening and life-changing injuries. He has been taken to hospital for treatment.
“Officers have attended the scene and have liaised with the Air Accident Investigation Branch.”
Hampshire fire service told The Sun: “Firefighters were called to a light aircraft crash at Popham Airfield at around six o’clock this evening.
“Crews from Rushmoor, Andover, Basingstoke and Winchester were alerted to the scene alongside police and ambulance teams.
“One casualty was released from the aircraft and passed into the care of paramedics.
“Firefighters made the aircraft safe, before the incident was handed over to police to manage the scene. Fire engines have begun to depart and return to station.”
South Central Ambulance added: “We received the 999 call at 17:43 for a microlite crash at Popham Airfield with reports of the pilot trapped. Our first crew on scene arrived at 17:59.
“Air ambulance and critical care doctors also attended. Police and Fire also attended.
“The patient, a 62 year old male, was freed and taken to Southampton Hospital at 19:02 by road ambulance.”
summary: A 62-year-old pilot sustained serious, potentially life-threatening injuries after his light aircraft overturned at Popham Airfield in Hampshire on Sunday evening. Emergency services, including police, firefighters, and paramedics, responded to the scene and freed the trapped pilot from the wreckage. He was subsequently transported by road ambulance to Southampton Hospital for treatment.
key_points: A 62-year-old pilot was seriously injured when his light aircraft overturned at Popham Airfield in Hampshire.
Emergency responders, including firefighters, freed the trapped pilot from the aircraft wreckage.
The patient was transported to Southampton Hospital by road ambulance with potentially life-threatening injuries.
Police and other emergency services attended the scene and liaised with the Air Accident Investigation Branch.

title: Labour mayors to force through plans for 4,000 new homes
author: Nick Gutteridge
content:
Sir James Cleverly, the shadow housing secretary, said: “While this Government announces new planning powers for mayors, it is simultaneously stripping councils across the country of their ability to make planning decisions in their own communities, while making it easier to build Traveller sites against local wishes.
“Worse still, Labour mayors have repeatedly failed to meet their housing targets, with Lord Sadiq Khan spectacularly missing his housebuilding targets year after year in London.
“The Conservatives are the only party with a plan to get Britain building and moving again with our plan to scrap stamp duty on the family home.”
Almost 1,900 new homes in the East Midlands that have been refused by local councils have been appealed to the planning inspectorate. They include plans for 420 new houses next to a railway yard in Broxtowe, Nottinghamshire, that were turned down by councillors but have now gone to appeal.
Claire Ward, the Labour metro Mayor for the East Midlands, has repeatedly called for more new homes to be built on such brownfield sites.
The planning inspectorate has also been called in after plans for 255 houses at Hetton, North Yorkshire, were rejected by the local council. Nearby plans for a 1,500-home development at Eggborough have been delayed by councillors, who now face the prospect of a planning appeal.
David Skaith, the Labour mayor for North Yorkshire, recently unveiled ambitious plans to build 60,000 new homes in the area, including 25,000 affordable houses.
Elsewhere, a 164-home development near Altofts in Wakefield has also been rejected by councillors and will now go to appeal.
Oliver Coppard, the Labour Mayor for South Yorkshire, has backed plans to build thousands of new homes on brownfield sites across the mayoralty.
summary: Labour metro mayors are pushing forward with plans for thousands of new homes, often focusing on brownfield sites, despite opposition from local councils. Numerous housing developments rejected or delayed by local authorities have been sent to the planning inspectorate for appeal. Meanwhile, Conservative shadow housing secretary Sir James Cleverly criticized the government's planning powers and Labour's past housing records.
key_points: Labour mayors are supporting large-scale housing developments on brownfield sites, including plans for 60,000 new homes in North Yorkshire.
Nearly 1,900 new homes in the East Midlands have been appealed to the planning inspectorate after being refused by local councils.
Projects in areas such as Broxtowe, North Yorkshire, and Wakefield face appeals or delays following council rejections.
Sir James Cleverly criticized Labour mayors for missing housing targets and accused the government of stripping planning powers from local councils.

title: How easy is it to find an NHS dentist? It depends on where you live
author: Chloe Hayward
content:
![Young female dentist and assistant working on female patient in chair](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/3e3c/live/56fd13c0-9d65-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
- Published
Hundreds of dentist practices are abandoning NHS work as the service drifts towards a two-tier system, new analysis suggests.
Data analysed by the Nuffield Trust found that nearly 600 practices in England have withdrawn from NHS dentistry over the last 10 years. The decline has been particularly sharp in parts of the South West and East of England, raising concerns about growing inequalities in access to care.
The analysis suggests more than one in 10 dental practices that once offered NHS care no longer do so, leaving it near impossible for some communities to find NHS appointments.
NHS dental activity is 8% lower than it was pre Covid, while six in 10 adults have not seen an NHS dentist in two years. Of those who attempted to get a new appointment in the last two years, just 38% were successful, according to a Nuffield Trust Survey.
![Map of England showing percentage change in the number of practices offering NHS dentistry, by Integrated Care Board area, March 2017 to March 2026](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/775b/live/ad96b970-9d65-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.png)
Cornwall, Devon and Northamptonshire have seen some of the biggest reductions in the number of practices offering NHS care. In Cornwall, more than a quarter of practices that previously offered NHS treatment have stopped doing so, making it one of the starkest examples of the shift away from NHS dentistry.
The findings come as ministers have pledged to tackle so-called "dental deserts", but dentists say the current deal is not viable. Many have handed back their NHS contracts because to work is loss-making.
In Somerset, fewer than one in five dental practices now offers NHS services. Alan, 83, who lives in the county, says he has given up trying to find an NHS dentist.
"I used to try, but getting a dental appointment anywhere near where I live would be impossible," he says.
Alan has only one tooth remaining after the others "crumbled out over the years" and says he has had to adapt what he eats, although he jokes that he has perfected a way of eating Brazil nuts.
![Close-up of Alan, 83, who has closely cropped grey hair and beard and wears large black-rimmed glasses.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1680/cpsprodpb/6349/live/4f9aca20-9d68-11f1-a07c-85afe5c51b6f.jpg)
Alan, 83, says he has given up trying to find an NHS dentist
Vivak Shah, who runs three dental practices in Northamptonshire, continues to offer NHS treatment but says it operates at a loss. He no longer takes on new NHS patients.
"Each year we struggle to decide what to do, and there is a limit to how much the private side can cover the NHS losses," says Shah.
He warned that if practices stop providing NHS treatment, many patients could be left in pain or forced to seek help elsewhere in the health service, including hospital accident and emergency departments.
"A contract handed back in one town attracts little national attention on its own but repeated across the country for a decade it amounts to the quiet transformation of dentistry into a two-tier service," says Mark Dayan, head of public affairs at the Nuffield Trust.
"Access to dental care increasingly depends on what people can afford to pay and where they live."
Jim Sykes is a dentist in Hexham. He handed back his NHS contract in 2024.
"It was a really hard emotional decision, but the NHS work was running at such a loss. I had to think of my team of staff and make it work," he says. Sykes asked if he could continue treating just children but was told he had to accept adults as well, or give up the NHS work.
"There has been a real breakdown in trust for me. Even if there was a new government offer, I would still be very nervous about entering a new NHS contract," he says.
![Photo of dentist Jim, a middle-aged man with fair hair and black-rimmed glasses. He's wearing scrubs and standing in a dental treatment room.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/c84b/live/fa84be90-9d64-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
Dentist Jim Sykes handed back his NHS contract in 2024 and says it was "a really hard emotional decision"
Sykes says that none of his friends in his graduating class in dentistry still works in the NHS. "My friends have gone private, retired or teach - any pathway to avoid NHS dentistry."
Shiv Pabary, chair of the British Dental Association's General Dental Practice Committee, says the situation is "the direct result of choices made by successive governments". He warns that unless ministers "fix and fund NHS dentistry", more dentists could choose to reduce their NHS work or leave the service altogether.
Overall dentist practice numbers have risen in England over the last decade.
"This is not a shortage of dentistry but a shortage of NHS dentistry," says Dayan. "Practices will need to be incentivised back into NHS work in the places where the NHS footprint has thinned most."
While most parts of England recorded declines in practices offering NHS dental care, the reductions were smallest in North West London, the Black Country and North East London.
North East London was the only area to see any increase during the period, recording one additional practice offering NHS treatment compared with a decade ago.
Every other region of England saw the number of NHS dental practices fall.
Looking at the number of practices doing NHS work is not the same as looking at exactly how much health service capacity there is - practices can vary in size. But if you look at other measures such as the amount of treatment being done, the numbers are still down, although not as steep as the fall in practice numbers.
The government says that it is changing the dental contract and training more dentists in the areas most in need. The government says it will also make it a requirement for newly qualified dentists to practice in the NHS for a minimum period of at least three years.
Campaign group 38 degrees calls the current dental crisis "shameful", with people being "forced to pay money they can't afford or suffer with the pain, shame, and further complications that come from being denied vital NHS healthcare".
- ![A treated image of a singular tooth with an infection. It is surrounded by dentistry tools.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/fc52/live/28ea5050-2769-11f1-934f-036468834728.jpg)
  - Published12 June
 ![A young man wearing glasses looks into the camera with a blurred Salford docks in the background](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/fcbc/live/dffc4bf0-65ac-11f1-8e1d-bbbb1017d210.jpg)
summary: Nearly 600 dental practices in England have withdrawn from NHS work over the last decade, leading to growing inequalities in access to care. Analysis by the Nuffield Trust shows that NHS dental activity is lower than pre-Covid levels, with only 38% of adults attempting to get a new appointment in the last two years succeeding. Dentists cite loss-making NHS contracts as the primary reason for abandoning the service, as the healthcare sector drifts toward an unaffordable two-tier system.
key_points: Nearly 600 practices in England have withdrawn from NHS dentistry over the last 10 years.
Only 38% of adults who tried to get a new dental appointment in the last two years were successful.
Cornwall, Devon, and Northamptonshire have experienced some of the sharpest reductions in NHS dental care.
Dentists argue that current NHS contracts are loss-making and force practices to abandon public work.
The government has pledged to change dental contracts, train more dentists, and require newly qualified dentists to practice in the NHS for at least three years.

title: Five arrested after rave broken up in Norfolk village
author: Ian Clarke
content:
Five people have been arrested and sound equipment seized after police shut down an unlicensed music event.
Police received reports shortly after 1am on Sunday near to Thursford Road, Little Snoring, near Fakenham.
Officers closed the entrance in order to prevent further people from attending.
They continued to monitor the event throughout the early hours of the morning.
Ravers were directed to leave the site under Section 63 of the Criminal Justice & Public Order Act 1994 and by late morning some of the attendees had begun to disperse.
Numerous vehicles, generators and sound equipment were seized by officers.
Police have launched an investigation in order to identify the organisers of the event and enquiries are ongoing.
Five people were arrested in connection with the event for offences including drug driving, drink driving, possession of a class A drugs with intent to supply and carrying on a licensable activity without a license.
Superintendent Craig Miller said: "Enquiries remain ongoing to determine the circumstances surrounding the unauthorised music event and to identify everyone involved in its organisation.
"We are committed to doing everything we can to prevent, disrupt and stop these events from taking place, while reducing their impact on local communities.
"I would like to thank the landowner and members of the local community for their patience and understanding while we worked to shut down the event as quickly and safely as possible.
"Unauthorised music events such as this can cause significant disruption and often result in damage to the natural environment. As they are not required to meet recognised safety standards, they can also place attendees at risk.
"Our work does not end with the closure of the event, and investigations into those responsible and the circumstances surrounding it will continue."
Patrick Galbraith, who lives in Great Snoring, went to to the rave site on Sunday morning.
He said: “The people at the rave were very friendly. A young raver apologised for snorting a white substance off his phone in front of me.”
Mr Galbraith added: “I later bumped into the police who said they could not 'go down there' without riot shields. This surprised me as there were not that many ravers.”
summary: Police in Norfolk shut down an unlicensed music event near Little Snoring on Sunday after receiving reports early in the morning. Officers seized sound equipment, generators, and vehicles while directing attendees to leave the site. Five individuals were arrested for various offenses, and an ongoing investigation has been launched to identify the event's organizers.
key_points: Five people were arrested following the closure of an unlicensed music event in Norfolk.
Police seized sound equipment, generators, and numerous vehicles from the site.
Attendees were directed to leave under Section 63 of the Criminal Justice & Public Order Act 1994.
Arrests included offenses such as drug driving, drink driving, and drug possession with intent to supply.
Authorities are continuing their investigation to identify the organizers of the rave.

title: Reform says it will prioritise British-born young workers for social housing
author: Henry Moore
content:
![Richard Tice, in blue jacket, white shirt, and black and white tie, points with his finger while talking to reporters](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/992/cpsprodpb/098c/live/b1e152d0-8819-11f1-981c-7d4dd1ef3d1d.jpg)
- Published
Reform UK has said it will prioritise British-born workers under 35 when allocating social housing if it were to enter government.
Deputy leader Richard Tice will set out plans to build 50,000 affordable social homes a year in a news conference on Monday, a policy which the party claims will require no new taxes or borrowing.
On top of British-born workers, former military service personnel and married couples with children will also be prioritised, Reform said.
A Labour spokesperson called the plans "unserious and unworkable" and accused Reform of pushing "gimmicks and division" with plans that "go after long-term UK residents that have contributed to our country".
Reform previously announced it would evict foreign nationals from social housing - a plan criticised by housing charity Shelter which said building more homes is the solution, rather than "changing the order of the queue" and "stoking division".
Tice will set out how the Reform intends to pay for the 50,000 affordable homes during Monday's news conference, the party added.
"It is time for us to prioritise young British workers, and that is what our policy is about," Tice said on Sunday.
"I have spent my entire career in property development, as a private citizen I have led companies which delivered thousands of new homes. In government I will break down the barriers to getting generation rent onto the housing ladder."
He added it is "time to get Britain building" and give "our young people the homes they deserve".
UK or Irish nationals made up 88.5% of main social home householders in 2024/25, according to the English Housing Survey.
That means around 11.5% of main householders, the perÂson in whose name the social home is renÂted, were non-UK or Irish nationÂals.
For its part, Reform estimates 540,000 social homes are currently occupied by foreign nationals.
Labour rubbished Reform's plans and insisted social housing is already "tightly controlled".
"Illegal migrants, asylum seekers and migrants on student or work visas are not eligible for social housing," the Labour spokesperson said.
Labour said the Reform plan would target long-term UK residents that have contributed to our country but are not British citizens, including NHS staff.
"It would leave more families at risk of homelessness and drive up use of temporary accommodation at the taxpayers' expense. It would also mean renegotiations with the EU, resulting in years of wrangling."
The Conservative Party, which also said it would revoke the right of foreign nationals to social housing, accused Reform of "trying to catch up" with its policies.
The Tories have said their plan, which would allow Irish citizens and some EU nationals to remain in social housing, would free up around 230,000 homes.
Sir James Cleverly, shadow housing secretary, added: "The Conservatives have already set out comprehensive plans to ensure British nationals are at the front of the queue for social housing. Now Reform are trying to catch up.
"We also believe in a home owning society and that those who work hard should be able to buy their own home, without unnecessary barriers standing in their way."
Liberal Democrat spokesperson Gideon Amos said that Reform's plan was a "cruel gimmick".
summary: Reform UK has announced plans to prioritise British-born workers under 35, former military personnel, and married couples with children for social housing if it enters government.
